prompt.context_jp: 埼玉県行田市の空はまだ寒く、その日、宮沢紘一___都心の百貨店バイヤー室の応接椅子に浅く腰かけていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮沢紘一___都心の百貨店バイヤー室の応接椅子に浅く腰かけていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Miyazawa as the established topic of this scene.

feedback.correct_en: Miyazawa is the already-known protagonist whose actions the narrative is tracking; は presents him as the topic ("as for Miyazawa, he was sitting...").
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new information, as if the reader didn't already know who the protagonist is. を is ungrammatical here—he's the sitter, not the object of an action.

contrast_examples.jp: 宮沢は椅子に腰かけていた。
contrast_examples.en: Miyazawa (as for him) was sitting in the chair.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かが椅子に腰かけていた。
contrast_examples.en: Someone (new information) was sitting in the chair.

prompt.context_jp: バイヤーが「ノーブランド」と言った直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: ノーブランドという言葉___、応接室の空気にざらりと沈殿する。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this word as newly impactful information.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence spotlights the word 'no-brand' as a fresh, striking element landing in the room. が marks this new, event-introducing subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the word as already-known topic, dulling its impact. に would mark a destination, which doesn't fit the subject role here.

contrast_examples.en: A heavy word fell (new, noticed).

contrast_examples.jp: その言葉は彼の口癖だった。
contrast_examples.en: That word was his habitual phrase (already-known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 半額や和装売り場という譲歩案を聞きながら。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妥協___できない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts 'compromise' with other possibilities.

feedback.correct_en: は singles out 妥協 for contrast: 'other things maybe—but compromise, no.' This fits Miyazawa's resolve against the buyer's concessions.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply name 'compromise' as the subject that can't be done, losing the implicit 'other things might be okay, but not this' nuance. を doesn't fit できる.

contrast_examples.en: Compromise (contrastively) is not something I can do.
I can't manage to compromise (plain inability, no contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢の信念。
prompt.prompt_jp: ランニングシューズは、ランニングシューズ売り場___こそ勝負しなければならない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks where the competition must take place.

feedback.correct_en: 勝負する is an action; で marks the location where that action takes place. こそ adds emphasis: 'precisely in the running-shoe section.'
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static location of existence or a destination, not where an action unfolds. を doesn't mark location at all.

contrast_examples.en: I fight here (action location).
I'm here (static existence).

prompt.context_jp: エレベーターの中、商談が終わって。
prompt.prompt_jp: 売り場___勝ち取れなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts this loss with what wasn't lost.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up contrast: he lost the shelf space, BUT (as the next sentence shows) his conviction didn't waver. The は primes the reader for the 'but' to come.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely state the fact without the contrastive setup. で (means/location) doesn't fit the direct-object slot here.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合は負けたが、気持ちは折れない。
contrast_examples.en: The match—we lost, but spirit isn't broken.
The match ended (plain report).

prompt.context_jp: 作業場で振り返る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茂木裕人___区間賞を取った瞬間の高揚が、いかにこの町工場全体を舞い上がらせていたか…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the subordinate clause describing when Mogi won.

feedback.correct_en: In a relative/subordinate clause describing an event ('the moment Mogi won'), が marks the subject. は is generally avoided inside such embedded clauses.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make Mogi the topic of the whole sentence, but here his winning is a specific past event embedded as a time modifier. を doesn't fit a subject role.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が勝った日は忘れられない。
contrast_examples.en: The day he won is unforgettable.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は勝った日を覚えている。
contrast_examples.en: He (topic) remembers the day he won.

prompt.context_jp: 重い空気の中、宮沢が社員に語りかける前。
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも口火を切る___、いつも宮沢の役だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that makes 'the one who breaks the ice' the topic being defined.

feedback.correct_en: The structure XのはYだった is a defining/presentational pattern: 'the one who did X was Y.' は marks the nominalized topic being characterized.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would fit if answering 'what was difficult/good' (e.g. 口火を切るのが難しい). のを would need a transitive verb like 待つ or 見る.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に話すのはいつも彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who always spoke first was him.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に話すのが難しい。
contrast_examples.en: Speaking first is the hard part.

prompt.context_jp: 640万円という数字が出た直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の空気___一瞬たわむ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this sudden, observed moment.

feedback.correct_en: This is a vivid, event-reporting sentence—the narrator notices a change happen. が presents the observation as new, in-the-moment information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the air' a known topic being commented on, flattening the sudden observational quality. に marks location, not subject.

contrast_examples.en: The air grew tense (noticed event).

contrast_examples.jp: 空気はいつも張り詰めている。
contrast_examples.en: The air is always tense (general characterization).

prompt.context_jp: 橘が毅然と断った後の小原の反応。
prompt.prompt_jp: 橘の毅然とした返事に、小原___わずかに目を細めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Obara as the topic reacting to Tachibana's reply.

feedback.correct_en: Obara is already an established character; the sentence tracks his reaction. は treats him as the known topic whose action is being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce him as new information, which clashes with his continuing presence. を doesn't fit a subject role.

contrast_examples.en: He (known) nodded.
Someone (new) nodded.

prompt.context_jp: 銀行で衝撃の報告を受けて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮沢の顔から___血の気が引き、テーブルの縁を握る手に力がこもった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after から that adds contrastive focus.

feedback.correct_en: からは contrastively singles out 'from the face' as the site of one change, parallel to 'the hand' tightening elsewhere. The は adds the implicit contrast between body parts.
feedback.incorrect_en: からが is ungrammatical/unnatural here. からで doesn't fit—で would mark means or location of action, not origin.

contrast_examples.jp: 目からは涙が、口からは笑いがあふれた。
contrast_examples.en: From the eyes tears, from the mouth laughter (contrastive pairing).
Tears fell from the eyes (plain).

prompt.context_jp: 坂本が相手先の名を告げた直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: アトランティス——その四文字___、部屋の空気を一気に凍りつかせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this dramatic, newly-landed subject.

feedback.correct_en: 'Those four letters' is being presented as a shocking new revelation whose impact is just hitting the room. が marks the newly-foregrounded subject causing the freeze.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'those four letters' as already-topical, draining the dramatic impact. を doesn't fit—the four letters are doing the freezing, not being frozen.

contrast_examples.jp: その名前が全員を黙らせた。
contrast_examples.en: That name silenced everyone (dramatic new agent).
That name is famous (general characterization).

prompt.context_jp: 橘の説明を宮沢が聞いた後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 橘の説明___静かで、そして揺るぎがなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that characterizes 'Tachibana's explanation' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: This is a characterization/evaluation of Tachibana's explanation as a whole. は presents it as the topic being described (quiet AND unwavering).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it feel like a sudden observation of a specific moment rather than a summary characterization. に doesn't fit the subject role.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の声は低くて落ち着いていた。
contrast_examples.en: His voice (as characterized) was low and calm.
A voice (new, suddenly) came from somewhere.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢の反論を受けた小原の変化。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小原の顔から、いつもの薄い笑み___消えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the observed disappearance.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reports a specific observed change: the smile vanished. が marks the subject of this noticed, in-the-moment event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require a contrast with another thing on his face that did stay—context doesn't support that. を is wrong because the smile is the one disappearing, not something being removed by an agent.

contrast_examples.en: The smile vanished (observed event).
The smile (contrastively) didn't vanish.

prompt.context_jp: バイヤーの提案に動揺を抑えて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮沢は膝に置いた手___わずかに握り直した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Miyazawa squeezed.

feedback.correct_en: 握り直す is a transitive verb and 手 is its direct object (what gets gripped again). を marks that object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the hand the subject doing the gripping, but Miyazawa is the agent. に would mark a destination, not the object being acted upon.

contrast_examples.en: To grip a hand (hand = object).
The hand goes numb (hand = subject).

prompt.context_jp: 廊下を歩きながら。
prompt.prompt_jp: 抱えた紙袋の陸王がこれ以上さらされないよう、そっと胸___寄せる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the destination of the gesture.

feedback.correct_en: 寄せる means to bring/draw something toward a point. に marks that goal/destination—the chest is where the bag is drawn to.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location of action (doing something at the chest), not a target. を would mark the chest as something traversed or acted upon.

contrast_examples.en: Draw it to one's body (target).
Hold it in the room (location of action).

prompt.context_jp: バイヤー室での張り詰めた場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼と担当者の間には、この一足の値打ちについての認識を揃えるための静かな緊張___張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing 'quiet tension' into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The 'quiet tension' is being introduced for the first time—a newly-perceived element in the scene. が presents this new descriptive subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that this tension is already known/topical. を doesn't fit—the tension is doing the taut-stretching itself (intransitive).

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に静かな緊張があった。
contrast_examples.en: There was quiet tension in the room (new presentation).

contrast_examples.jp: その緊張はしばらく続いた。
contrast_examples.en: That tension (now known) lasted a while.

prompt.context_jp: 売り場を取れなかった後の宮沢の心境。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが、それでも陸王がいかなる場所で戦うべきかについて___、少しも揺らいでいなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the topic of what wasn't wavering.

feedback.correct_en: についてはX pattern: 'as for X, [comment].' は picks out this specific topic—the question of where Rikuoh should fight—and contrasts it with everything else that did waver.
feedback.incorrect_en: についてが is ungrammatical in this slot. についてを doesn't fit—についてis already a prepositional phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: それについては考えが変わらない。
contrast_examples.en: As for that, my thinking hasn't changed.
That is the problem (plain subject).

prompt.context_jp: バイヤーが半額を提案する理由。
prompt.prompt_jp: こはぜ屋さんにはシューズメーカーとしての___がありませんから…
prompt.prompt_en: What does the buyer say Kohazeya lacks as a shoe maker?

feedback.correct_en: The buyer's complaint is about brand recognition, not money or craftsmanship. ブランド力 ('brand power') is the exact noun used to criticize Kohazeya's standing in the shoe market.
feedback.incorrect_en: 資金力 (financial strength) and 技術力 (technical skill) would send a different message—especially 技術力, since Kohazeya is actually very skilled. The missing piece is market presence as a shoe brand.

contrast_examples.jp: うちはブランド力で勝てない。
contrast_examples.en: We can't win on brand power.
In technical skill, we won't lose.

prompt.context_jp: 村野が宮沢に突きつける選択肢。
prompt.prompt_jp: 売れないのなら 売れる方法を考えるか ___ やめるかです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb that intensifies 'quit' into a clean, decisive exit.

feedback.correct_en: きっぱり pairs with やめる to mean 'quit cleanly/decisively without lingering'—exactly the stark binary Murano is forcing: fix it, or walk away cleanly.
feedback.incorrect_en: ゆっくりやめる ('slowly quit') makes no sense in a decisive ultimatum. うっかり ('carelessly') contradicts the deliberate framing of a business decision.

contrast_examples.en: To refuse decisively.
To carelessly forget.

prompt.context_jp: 橘がアトランティスの大量注文について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 正直 アトランティスからの 大量ロット注文は ___ほど欲しい
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom expressing intense craving.

feedback.correct_en: 喉から手が出るほど欲しい is a set idiom: 'wanting something so badly that a hand would come out of your throat (to grab it).' Perfect for the desperate pull Atlantis's offer has on Tachibana.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目が飛び出る describes shock (especially at prices). 耳が痛い means a criticism hits uncomfortably close to home—neither expresses desire.

contrast_examples.jp: 喉から手が出るほど欲しい。
contrast_examples.en: I want it so badly my hand would come out my throat.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段を見て目が飛び出た。
contrast_examples.en: My eyes popped out at the price.

prompt.context_jp: 小原が宮沢に反論する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大企業の何たるかを あなたに どうこう言われる ___などない！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun meaning 'no grounds / no business to.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜筋合いはない means 'you have no grounds/standing to [say/do] this.' Obara is denying Miyazawa's right to lecture him about big-corporation ethics.
feedback.incorrect_en: 都合 means convenience/circumstances; 具合 means condition/state. Neither carries the sense of 'standing to criticize' that the context demands.

contrast_examples.jp: 君に言われる筋合いはない。
contrast_examples.en: You have no standing to say that to me.
It's inconvenient.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢がアトランティスの動機を試す言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: もしも私たちを潰すためだけに 今回の契約を結ばれたというなら 私は あなた方を 心の底から___するところでした
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb expressing deep contempt from the bottom of one's heart.

feedback.correct_en: 軽蔑する = 'to despise/hold in contempt.' Pairs naturally with 心の底から ('from the bottom of my heart') to convey how low Miyazawa would rank them if they were purely malicious.
feedback.incorrect_en: 尊敬 (respect) and 感謝 (gratitude) are the opposite emotions and would make nonsense of the conditional 'if you were just trying to crush us.'

contrast_examples.jp: 彼を心の底から軽蔑する。
contrast_examples.en: I despise him from the bottom of my heart.
I truly respect him.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が橘に最後の宣告をする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 3月以降は どんなことがあっても もう二度と 御社とは取り引きはしません ___だ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that intensifies 'never ever again.'

feedback.correct_en: 金輪際 is an emphatic adverb meaning 'absolutely never (again),' used almost exclusively with negative statements. It seals Miyazawa's vow with Buddhist-rooted finality.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一瞬 means 'a brief moment'—opposite in nuance. 一応 means 'for now / tentatively,' which would utterly undermine the finality Miyazawa is declaring.

contrast_examples.en: I'll never ever forgive this.
I'll just confirm for now.

prompt.context_jp: 選手が陸王を履いた直後の感想。
prompt.prompt_jp: 軽いなんて そんな___じゃないですよ 自分の足そのものですよ このシューズ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that means 'level / dimension' in this intensified praise.

feedback.correct_en: そんな次元じゃない is a set phrase meaning 'it's on a totally different level/plane than that.' The athlete is saying 'light' doesn't even begin to capture the sensation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時代 (era) and 方向 (direction) don't form this collocation; the idiom specifically uses 次元 (dimension/level) for 'beyond that category.'

contrast_examples.jp: そんな次元の話じゃない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not even on that level.
It's a different era.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢と大地が去った後、橘の心の動き。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼の中で崩れかけていた___が、ようやく釣り合いを取り戻そうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the metaphorical noun for a balance being restored.

feedback.correct_en: 天秤 ('scales/balance') is the natural metaphor for weighing competing choices—money vs. loyalty. It collocates directly with 釣り合いを取り戻す ('regain balance').
feedback.incorrect_en: 鏡 (mirror) and 柱 (pillar) don't fit the 'weighing two options' image; a mirror reflects, a pillar supports, but neither is 'in balance.'

contrast_examples.en: The scales of one's heart tip.
The pillar of one's heart breaks.

prompt.context_jp: エレベーターの中、宮沢の内面を描く地の文として。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as narration right after Miyazawa fails to secure the shelf space?

choices.text: 売り場は勝ち取れなかった。だが、それでも陸王がいかなる場所で戦うべきかについては、少しも揺らいでいなかった。
売り場が勝ち取れなかった。だが、それでも陸王がいかなる場所で戦うべきかについてが、少しも揺らいでいなかった。

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses は in both clauses to set up contrast ('the shelf — lost; but his conviction — unshaken'). This parallel contrastive は is what gives the narration its weight.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B's が makes 売り場 a plain subject and renders ついてが ungrammatical. The contrastive 'yes-but' structure needs は on both sides.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合は負けた。だが心は折れていない。
contrast_examples.en: The match — we lost. But the spirit — not broken.
(Unnatural without context setup.)

prompt.context_jp: 橘が「取引先の規模は関係ない」と語る場面として。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural in Tachibana's assertion?

choices.text: 相手がどんな会社であろうと、大切な顧客に変わりはありません。
相手がどんな会社でも、大切な顧客は変わっていません。

feedback.correct_en: 〜に変わりはない is a fixed expression meaning 'the fact remains unchanged.' Combined with であろうと ('no matter what...'), it carries firm, formal business conviction.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B's 変わっていません describes a past-to-present process ('they haven't changed'), which misses the point—Tachibana is making a principled statement about status, not tracking change over time.

contrast_examples.jp: 小さくても大切な顧客に変わりはない。
contrast_examples.en: Small or not, it remains a valued client.

contrast_examples.jp: 顧客は変わっていない。
contrast_examples.en: The clients haven't changed (over time).

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が「金のためだけの仕事」と「共に挑む仕事」の違いを説く場面として。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for Miyazawa's point about shared work?

choices.text: そこには絆が生まれる。その絆が次のビジネスチャンスを生むんです。
そこで絆を生みます。その絆で次のビジネスチャンスを生みます。

feedback.correct_en: 絆が生まれる (bonds are born / arise) is the natural intransitive collocation—bonds emerge of their own accord from shared struggle. が marks this spontaneous appearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B's 絆を生む treats bonds as something manufactured by will. It sounds mechanical and misses the organic 'bonds just happen when you work together' meaning Miyazawa is building.

contrast_examples.en: Trust is born (naturally arises).
Effort to generate trust (deliberate).

prompt.context_jp: 作業場での自戒の地の文として。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as the narrator's reflection?

choices.text: 売れる、という言葉に酔ったのは、決して社長ひとりの罪ではない。
売れる、という言葉に酔ったのが、決して社長ひとりの罪ではない。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のは〜だ cleft structure introduces 'the one who got drunk on the word 'sell'' as the topic being characterized. は is correct for this defining pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would normally pair with evaluative/sensory predicates (〜のが好きだ, 〜のが見える). With 罪ではない ('isn't a sin'), は is what cleftly defines whose action it was.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に気づいたのは彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who first noticed was him.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が気づくのが遅かった。
contrast_examples.en: His noticing was late.
